SMTO-HTTP-0031 — The service SMTO tried to reach turned the connection away

GUID: 726beddf-f70a-4cd8-8c55-ba5b0f4aae54
Slug: http-connection-refused
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO's Gateway reached the computer at that address, but nothing there was accepting connections. The request was not delivered.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the service you want SMTO to use is running. For example, open its web page in a browser on the Gateway's computer. A refused connection usually means the service is stopped or still starting up.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select the HTTP connection, and check Base URL, especially http or https and the port number after the colon (such as :8080). The right computer with the wrong port number turns the connection away.
  3. If a proxy is set under Advanced connection settings, make sure that proxy is running and its address is correct. A stopped proxy refuses connections in exactly the same way.
  4. Select Test connection. When it shows Reachable, run the task again. Once the service accepts connections, sending the request again is safe.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Reachable and the task's request gets an answer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to whoever runs the service or your network; a firewall may be blocking the Gateway's computer. Don't remove saved data or turn off security checks on the connection to work around it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's TCP connection attempt to the destination (or configured proxy) host and port failed with ConnectionRefusedError; no listener accepted the connection.

What this means

  • The transport exception chain contains ConnectionRefusedError from a connection attempt. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The transport exception chain contains ConnectionRefusedError from a connection attempt.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the actual destination or configured proxy listener and port; do not assume the application received the request.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the destination service is running and listening on the host and port in the profile's base_url (and any configured proxy), and check firewalls between the Gateway host and the target, for example with curl -v from the Gateway host.
  • Start or correct the destination listener and verify the host and port.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended route accepts the connection and a bounded read confirms reachability.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
